title: A 150-point no-three-in-line configuration on a 75 by 75 grid
statement: Does there exist S contained in {0,...,74}^2 with |S|=150 such that (x_j-x_i)(y_k-y_i)-(x_k-x_i)(y_j-y_i) is nonzero for every three distinct points of S? A construction attains the row-count upper bound; an impossibility proof must cover all configurations.
source_locator: Introduction and maintained frontier entries for n=71,73,74,76; summary-table date 2026-09-11.
status_basis: The author-maintained frontier records all sizes 2 through 74 and size 76, but no size 75. Searches for a size-75 construction or impossibility result found no authoritative resolution by 2026-10-14. This is an open-status inference from a dated frontier gap, not an explicit theorem of open status.

epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No physical model, empirical data or experiment is needed.

difficulty.basis: The unrestricted target is a research frontier; a bounded trial has no assured outcome.

correctness.basis: No project candidate solution has been submitted or independently reviewed.

plain_summary: Place 150 lattice points on a 75 by 75 board so that no straight line contains three. A finite output is easy to check independently, although finding it may be hard.
assumptions: Coordinates are integers from 0 to 74 inclusive.
Collinearity includes every slope, not just rows, columns and main diagonals.
All points must be distinct; a tolerance-based drawing is insufficient.
scope: The unrestricted size-75 existence question. A separately proposed first milestone examines half-turn invariant configurations; this is a curator-designed restriction, not a reduction of the whole problem.
target: Find a 150-point witness, or prove none exists. First milestone: encode configurations invariant under (x,y) -> (74-x,74-y), provide the exact constraints, and conduct one capped search.
success_criteria: Supply all 150 integer pairs and pass an independently written determinant checker.
For the proposed milestone, require two points in every row and column, half-turn invariance, and at most two points on every grid line; declare any further restrictions.
Cap the proposed milestone at 8 CPU-hours and 16 GiB RAM. These are chosen limits, not measured requirements or predicted time to success.
A checked UNSAT certificate for the restricted encoding establishes only absence in that subclass. A timeout establishes neither existence nor nonexistence.
known_results: The maintained source records constructions at all sizes 2 through 74 and at 76; size 75 is absent in the inspected frontier.
The elementary row argument gives at most 150 points. No independently audited best sub-150 value is asserted.
significance: A witness closes a gap below the largest recorded solved board. An obstruction for a precisely specified symmetry class may guide searches, subject to a separate novelty check.

requirements.data: Self-contained. Optional attributed configurations and encodings come from Flammenkamp's database.
requirements.compute: Proposed cap: 8 CPU-hours and 16 GiB RAM. The grid has 5,625 positions. A positive witness needs C(150,3)=551,300 exact triple checks. Full impossibility may require much larger resources.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Euclidean collinearity of integer points. Half-turn symmetry is a voluntary search restriction, not a theorem about optimal configurations.

ai_assessment.rationale: Priority applies to the bounded construction experiment: its output is precise and independently checkable. It does not predict that the frontier target will be solved.

clarity.reason: The board, point count and predicate are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Encoding, symmetry, search and checking separate naturally.

methods.reason: The source documents constraint searches and reusable symmetry records.

search_or_symbolic.reason: The predicates are finite exact integer constraints.

checkability.reason: A positive witness requires a modest number of determinant checks.

expertise.reason: Search design needs experience; the witness checker is elementary.

significance.reason: A witness fills an actively maintained finite frontier gap.

verification_difficulty.reason: Positive checking is simple; UNSAT needs an encoding proof and certificate audit.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model or search has been evaluated. Easy checking gives no estimate of success probability, and the frontier can change quickly.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI able to implement integer constraints, reason about symmetry and produce inspectable solver inputs.

methods: SAT or constraint programming with line-capacity constraints
Local search guided by collinear triples
obstacles: A symmetry restriction may remove every solution.
Checking only familiar slopes changes the problem.
Existing unpublished searches may cover the restricted case.
A 149-point output is not automatically a new record; the database primarily records full configurations.

steps: Check count, distinctness and coordinate bounds independently.
Enumerate every triple with exact integer arithmetic and reject zero determinants.
For a solver proof, reconstruct the constraints and use an independent certificate verifier.
Refresh the source before a novelty claim.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Low for a positive witness; high for a global impossibility proof.
validation.statement_alignment: The main statement covers all configurations; the half-turn milestone cannot establish unrestricted nonexistence.

known_attempts: The maintained collection attributes recent frontier constructions to Thomas Prellberg, Mitchell Riley and Marijn Heule; it lists no size-75 solution.
unresolved_checks: Determine whether the proposed symmetry case has already been exhausted.
Audit sub-150 records before claiming a lower-count improvement.
